ai.description: *Raorchestes vellikkannan* is a small shrub frog (20–25 mm) with a distinct metallic silver iris. Its body is yellowish-brown with irregular dark markings and translucent, pale-edged limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes vellikkannan* is uniquely distinguished from similar congeners by its striking, distinctively bright silvery-white iris, which contrasts sharply with its body.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes vellikkannan* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen cloud forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Silver-eyed Shrub Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among foliage during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes vellikkannan* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of eggs in leaf axils during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes vellikkannan* is endemic to the high-elevation cloud forests of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found above 1,700 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Raorchestes vellikkannan* produces a high-pitched, insect-like series of short, rhythmic chirps heard primarily from shrubs within its high-altitude forest habitat.
